content: The document discusses various strategies and guidelines for improving school health services (SHS) and adolescent health globally. It highlights innovative approaches such as task-sharing and mobile clinics to enhance service delivery. The implementation of the World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines on SHS is emphasized, with references to evidence-based frameworks and tools. Key references include the GRADE guidelines for assessing evidence quality, WHO's handbook for guideline development, and global standards for health-promoting schools. The WHO and UNESCO have collaborated on initiatives to make every school a health-promoting institution, focusing on improving student health, well-being, and academic outcomes. The Global Accelerated Action for the Health of Adolescents (AA-HA.) framework provides country-specific guidance for adolescent health interventions. The document also references studies on the effectiveness of school-based health centers in addressing health disparities, improving academic performance, and managing chronic conditions like asthma and mental health issues. It underscores the importance of comprehensive school health programs, including nutrition, physical activity, sexual and reproductive health education, and mental health support. Additionally, the document includes guidelines for addressing barriers to adolescent health services, ensuring equity, and promoting universal health coverage. The references span a wide range of topics, including child and adolescent injury prevention, vaccination strategies, oral health promotion, and the prevention of early pregnancy. The WHO's technical reports and position papers provide detailed recommendations for implementing effective health interventions in schools, particularly in low-resource settings. Overall, the document serves as a comprehensive resource for policymakers, educators, and healthcare providers aiming to enhance the quality and accessibility of school health services worldwide.
